channel.title: The Colombo Court blog
channel.description: Notes on Colombo, the hotel, the spa and the two restaurants, from Colombo Court Hotel & Spa in Colombo 3.

item.title: Where to eat in Colombo 3, from the people at the desk
item.description: The honest version of the question we are asked most. What is worth walking to in Kollupitiya, what is worth a tuk-tuk, and what to do about Sunday nights.

item.title: Getting from Bandaranaike airport to Colombo 3
item.description: Thirty-five kilometres, forty-five minutes to an hour, and four ways to do it. What each costs, what to do about a three in the morning arrival, and where to change money.

item.title: High tea in Colombo, and when to go
item.description: What high tea actually means in a country that grows the tea, what goes on the stand, what it costs here, and the ninety minutes of the day worth booking it for.

item.title: What a carbon neutral hotel actually does
item.description: We have been certified CarbonNeutral since 2011, which was the first for a city hotel in South Asia. Here is what that involves in a building, rather than in a brochure.

item.title: The best time to visit Sri Lanka, and why the answer is two answers
item.description: The island has two monsoons running at opposite ends of the year, so there is no bad season, only a wrong coast. Month by month, where to be and what it costs.

item.title: Two days in Colombo, without rushing
item.description: Most people give Colombo one night on the way to somewhere else. Two days is enough to see why that is a mistake, and this is the order we would do it in.

item.title: Things to do in Colombo 3, on foot
item.description: Kollupitiya is the strip between Galle Road and the sea, and almost everything worth doing in it is within a twenty minute walk. Here is what, and in what order.

item.title: Balinese or Ayurvedic: which massage to book
item.description: They are not variations on the same hour. One works on muscle and the other works on the whole system, and the right question is what you actually want to leave feeling.

item.title: A Sri Lankan breakfast, explained
item.description: Hoppers, string hoppers, pol sambol, kiribath and a curry before eight in the morning. What each thing is, how to eat it, and why it is worth getting up for.

item.title: Why our rooms face inward
item.description: Every window here looks into a planted court rather than out at the city. That was not an aesthetic decision to begin with. It was the only way the building worked.

item.title: Working from Colombo, honestly assessed
item.description: The internet, the time zone, the power situation and where to actually sit. A straight answer for anyone thinking of running a week of work from Sri Lanka.

item.title: Colombo when it rains, which is often
item.description: Two monsoons, neither of them a washout. What the rain here actually does, what to do with the hour it takes, and why the wet months are the ones to book.

item.title: How many days do you need in Colombo?
item.description: One night, two days or four? An honest answer for a city that most people treat as an airport with a hotel attached, from people who would rather you enjoyed it.

item.title: Getting around Colombo: tuk-tuks, apps and the coastal train
item.description: What each way of moving costs, when the traffic makes walking faster, how to avoid being overcharged, and the one train journey worth planning a morning around.

item.title: What to pack for Sri Lanka, and what to leave behind
item.description: Thirty degrees and humid every day, temples with a dress code, fierce air conditioning indoors and rain that arrives in a rush. A short list that assumes you can buy anything you forget.

item.title: Is Colombo worth visiting? A straight answer
item.description: It is not a city of monuments, it does not photograph like Galle, and half the guidebooks tell you to skip it. Here is the honest case for and against, from people with an obvious interest.

item.title: A short guide to Ceylon tea
item.description: Why the country is called Sri Lanka and the tea is still called Ceylon, what the growing altitudes actually taste like, and how to buy some without being sold floor sweepings.

item.title: Your first spa visit, and what nobody tells you
item.description: What to wear, what happens to your clothes, how much pressure to ask for and whether to talk. The awkward questions, answered plainly, so the hour is not spent wondering.

item.title: What to look for in an eco-friendly hotel in Colombo
item.description: Every hotel in Colombo now has a green claim, and few of them can be checked. Here are the questions that separate a genuine one from a laminated promise, including the ones we would find awkward.

item.title: A wedding or an event in Colombo, and what to ask before you book
item.description: Capacities, the monsoon question, what a venue should tell you without being asked, and the case for a small wedding in a garden rather than a large one in a ballroom.
